claims.text: Validated tools: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) or Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ).
claims.quote: Clinicians may use validated instruments such as the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) or the "Ask Suicide-Screening Questions" (ASQ) tool developed by the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH).

claims.text: Assess the mental state for depression, anxiety, agitation, panic attacks, severe insomnia, other mental disorders and alcohol or drug use disorders.
claims.quote: Fully assessing the patient’s mental state, with particular emphasis on identifying depression, anxiety, agitation, panic attacks, severe insomnia, other mental disorders, and alcohol or drug use disorders

claims.text: Ask about firearms and other lethal means at home, and counsel on safe storage.
claims.quote: Inquiring about the presence of a firearm or other lethal means in the house and providing lethal means counseling (this may involve facilitating the safe storage or disposal of lethal means away from the home)
Interviewing close family members and friends

claims.text: Treat any serious self-injury and assess suicide risk.
claims.quote: Every person with a serious self-injury should be evaluated and treated for the physical injury and assessed for suicide risk.

claims.text: After an ingestion: acetaminophen level in every mixed ingestion.
claims.quote: Many authorities recommend measuring acetaminophen levels in all patients with mixed ingestions

claims.text: Delirium, seizures or fever may need medical admission with suicide precautions.
claims.quote: Patients with manifestations of potentially confounding medical disorders (eg, delirium, seizures, fever) may need to be admitted to a medical unit with appropriate suicide precautions.
